Subject-wise Grades: Carefully check the grades obtained in each subject. Qualifying Status: Confirm whether the result shows the candidate as qualified. Original Marksheet: The original marksheet will be distributed by the respective schools at a later date.

hindi_script: पंजाब स्कूल एजुकेशन बोर्ड ने जुलाई 2026 में आयोजित हुई 10वीं कक्षा की सप्लीमेंट्री परीक्षा का परिणाम घोषित कर दिया है। जो छात्र नियमित बोर्ड परीक्षा में उत्तीर्ण नहीं हो पाए थे या अपना प्रदर्शन सुधारना चाहते थे, वे आधिकारिक वेबसाइट pseb.ac.in पर जाकर अपना रिजल्ट देख सकते हैं। ऑनलाइन परिणाम जांचने के लिए उम्मीदवारों को वेबसाइट के रिजल्ट सेक्शन में 'Result of Matriculation Supplementary Examination, July 2026' लिंक पर क्लिक करके अपना रोल नंबर दर्ज करना होगा, जिसके बाद स्क्रीन पर दिख रही प्रोविजनल मार्कशीट को डाउनलोड कर उसका प्रिंटआउट लिया जा सकता है। अत्यधिक ट्रैफिक के कारण वेबसाइट न खुलने पर छात्र एसएमएस सेवा का उपयोग कर सकते हैं। इसके लिए मोबाइल के मैसेज ऐप में PB10 के बाद अपना रोल नंबर टाइप करके 5676750 पर भेजना होगा, जिससे रिजल्ट पंजीकृत मोबाइल नंबर पर प्राप्त हो जाएगा। छात्र अपने स्कोरकार्ड में नाम, रोल नंबर, विषयवार ग्रेड और क्वालीफाइंग स्टेटस का मिलान कर लें। वहीं, मूल मार्कशीट बाद में संबंधित स्कूलों द्वारा प्रदान की जाएगी।

script: पंजाब स्कूल एजुकेशन बोर्ड ने जुलाई 2026 में आयोजित हुई 10वीं कक्षा की सप्लीमेंट्री परीक्षा का परिणाम घोषित कर दिया है। जो छात्र नियमित बोर्ड परीक्षा में उत्तीर्ण नहीं हो पाए थे या अपना प्रदर्शन सुधारना चाहते थे, वे आधिकारिक वेबसाइट pseb.ac.in पर जाकर अपना रिजल्ट देख सकते हैं। ऑनलाइन परिणाम जांचने के लिए उम्मीदवारों को वेबसाइट के रिजल्ट सेक्शन में 'Result of Matriculation Supplementary Examination, July 2026' लिंक पर क्लिक करके अपना रोल नंबर दर्ज करना होगा, जिसके बाद स्क्रीन पर दिख रही प्रोविजनल मार्कशीट को डाउनलोड कर उसका प्रिंटआउट लिया जा सकता है। अत्यधिक ट्रैफिक के कारण वेबसाइट न खुलने पर छात्र एसएमएस सेवा का उपयोग कर सकते हैं। इसके लिए मोबाइल के मैसेज ऐप में PB10 के बाद अपना रोल नंबर टाइप करके 5676750 पर भेजना होगा, जिससे रिजल्ट पंजीकृत मोबाइल नंबर पर प्राप्त हो जाएगा। छात्र अपने स्कोरकार्ड में नाम, रोल नंबर, विषयवार ग्रेड और क्वालीफाइंग स्टेटस का मिलान कर लें। वहीं, मूल मार्कशीट बाद में संबंधित स्कूलों द्वारा प्रदान की जाएगी।

title: Aurobindo Pharma US FDA Inspection Ends With 3 Observations At Apitoria Pharma Plant
teaser: Aurobindo Pharma on Friday said a US Food and Drug Administration (US FDA) inspection at an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing facility operated by its wholly owned subsidiary Apitoria Pharma concluded with three observati
description: Aurobindo Pharma on Friday said a US Food and Drug Administration (US FDA) inspection at an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing facility operated by its wholly owned subsidiary Apitoria Pharma concluded with three observati
content: Aurobindo Pharma on Friday said a US Food and Drug Administration (US FDA) inspection at an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing facility operated by its wholly owned subsidiary Apitoria Pharma concluded with three observations. The inspection was conducted from August 24 to August 28 at Unit-VI of Apitoria Pharma in E-Bonangi Village, Parawada Mandal, in Andhra Pradesh’s Anakapalli district. The pharmaceutical company described all three observations as procedural in nature and said it would submit its response to the US FDA within the prescribed timeline. Aurobindo Pharma did not provide details about the specific observations. Read Also Mumbai: FDA Cracks Down On Vendors Using Newspapers For Food Packaging, Fines 26 Establishments FDA Inspection Follows Another Facility Review FPJ Shorts Aurobindo Pharma US FDA Inspection Ends With 3 Observations At Apitoria Pharma Plant SBI PO Prelims Result 2026 Declared At sbi.bank.in; Mains Exam On September 12 Maharashtra: Student Made To Stand In Class, Parent Allegedly Assaults Doctor At Beed Medical Institute; Video Viral Govt Dismisses CBG Price Hike Concerns, Says CNG, PNG Impact Minimal An FDA observation indicates that inspectors have identified conditions that may not fully comply with regulatory requirements. However, such observations do not automatically constitute final regulatory action, and companies are generally given an opportunity to respond and undertake corrective measures. Aurobindo Pharma said it continues to focus on maintaining quality and regulatory compliance across its manufacturing operations and will update stock exchanges about material developments as required. The latest inspection comes just days after another Aurobindo Pharma subsidiary, AuroPeptides Ltd, underwent a separate US FDA review. Four Observations Across Two Subsidiaries The AuroPeptides facility in Indrakaran Village, Kandi Mandal, Telangana, was inspected between August 17 and August 21. The site manufactures peptide APIs, and the inspection concluded with one observation. Aurobindo Pharma had earlier said corrective measures were initiated during that inspection and that a formal response would be submitted within the required timeframe. Together, the two inspections have resulted in four observations across facilities operated by two subsidiaries within one week. While Aurobindo has characterised the latest three observations as procedural, it has not disclosed the specific findings from either inspection. Aurobindo Pharma shares closed 0.92% higher at ₹1,652 on Friday, gaining ₹15 during the session.

hindi_script: अरबिंदो फार्मा की पूर्ण स्वामित्व वाली सहायक कंपनी एपिटोरिया फार्मा के आंध्र प्रदेश स्थित एक्टिव फार्मास्युटिकल इंग्रेडिएंट यानी एपीआई विनिर्माण संयंत्र में अमरीकी खाद्य एवं औषधि प्रशासन (US FDA) का निरीक्षण तीन आपत्तियों के साथ समाप्त हुआ है। यह जांच अनाकापल्ली जिले के परवड़ा मंडल स्थित ई-बोनंगी गांव में एपिटोरिया फार्मा की यूनिट-VI में 24 अगस्त से 28 अगस्त तक की गई थी। फार्मा कंपनी ने इन तीनों आपत्तियों को प्रक्रियात्मक प्रकृति का बताया है और कहा है कि वह निर्धारित समय सीमा के भीतर US FDA को अपना जवाब सौंपेगी, हालांकि कंपनी ने विशिष्ट आपत्तियों का विवरण साझा नहीं किया है। नियमों के तहत US FDA की आपत्तियां उन स्थितियों को दर्शाती हैं जो नियामक आवश्यकताओं का पूरी तरह पालन नहीं करती हैं, लेकिन ये स्वचालित रूप से अंतिम कार्रवाई नहीं होतीं और कंपनियों को सुधारात्मक कदम उठाने का मौका दिया जाता है। अरबिंदो फार्मा ने कहा है कि वह अपने विनिर्माण कार्यों में गुणवत्ता और अनुपालन बनाए रखेगी तथा जरूरी होने पर स्टॉक एक्सचेंजों को सूचित करेगी। यह निरीक्षण अरबिंदो फार्मा की एक अन्य सहायक कंपनी अरोपैप्टाइड्स लिमिटेड की समीक्षा के तुरंत बाद हुआ है। तेलंगाना के कांडी मंडल स्थित इंद्रकरण गांव में पेप्टाइड एपीआई बनाने वाली अरोपैप्टाइड्स की इकाई का निरीक्षण 17 अगस्त से 21 अगस्त के बीच हुआ था, जो एक आपत्ति के साथ समाप्त हुआ था। उस समय भी कंपनी ने सुधारात्मक उपाय शुरू करने और तय समय में औपचारिक जवाब देने की बात कही थी। इस तरह एक ही सप्ताह के भीतर कंपनी की दो सहायक इकाइयों के संयंत्रों में कुल चार आपत्तियां सामने आई हैं। इन घटनाक्रमों के बीच शुक्रवार को शेयर बाजार में अरबिंदो फार्मा का शेयर 0.92 प्रतिशत यानी 15 रुपये की बढ़त के साथ 1,652 रुपये पर बंद हुआ।

script: अरबिंदो फार्मा की पूर्ण स्वामित्व वाली सहायक कंपनी एपिटोरिया फार्मा के आंध्र प्रदेश स्थित एक्टिव फार्मास्युटिकल इंग्रेडिएंट यानी एपीआई विनिर्माण संयंत्र में अमरीकी खाद्य एवं औषधि प्रशासन (US FDA) का निरीक्षण तीन आपत्तियों के साथ समाप्त हुआ है। यह जांच अनाकापल्ली जिले के परवड़ा मंडल स्थित ई-बोनंगी गांव में एपिटोरिया फार्मा की यूनिट-VI में 24 अगस्त से 28 अगस्त तक की गई थी। फार्मा कंपनी ने इन तीनों आपत्तियों को प्रक्रियात्मक प्रकृति का बताया है और कहा है कि वह निर्धारित समय सीमा के भीतर US FDA को अपना जवाब सौंपेगी, हालांकि कंपनी ने विशिष्ट आपत्तियों का विवरण साझा नहीं किया है। नियमों के तहत US FDA की आपत्तियां उन स्थितियों को दर्शाती हैं जो नियामक आवश्यकताओं का पूरी तरह पालन नहीं करती हैं, लेकिन ये स्वचालित रूप से अंतिम कार्रवाई नहीं होतीं और कंपनियों को सुधारात्मक कदम उठाने का मौका दिया जाता है। अरबिंदो फार्मा ने कहा है कि वह अपने विनिर्माण कार्यों में गुणवत्ता और अनुपालन बनाए रखेगी तथा जरूरी होने पर स्टॉक एक्सचेंजों को सूचित करेगी। यह निरीक्षण अरबिंदो फार्मा की एक अन्य सहायक कंपनी अरोपैप्टाइड्स लिमिटेड की समीक्षा के तुरंत बाद हुआ है। तेलंगाना के कांडी मंडल स्थित इंद्रकरण गांव में पेप्टाइड एपीआई बनाने वाली अरोपैप्टाइड्स की इकाई का निरीक्षण 17 अगस्त से 21 अगस्त के बीच हुआ था, जो एक आपत्ति के साथ समाप्त हुआ था। उस समय भी कंपनी ने सुधारात्मक उपाय शुरू करने और तय समय में औपचारिक जवाब देने की बात कही थी। इस तरह एक ही सप्ताह के भीतर कंपनी की दो सहायक इकाइयों के संयंत्रों में कुल चार आपत्तियां सामने आई हैं। इन घटनाक्रमों के बीच शुक्रवार को शेयर बाजार में अरबिंदो फार्मा का शेयर 0.92 प्रतिशत यानी 15 रुपये की बढ़त के साथ 1,652 रुपये पर बंद हुआ।

title: Rahul Gandhi demands FIR under SC/ST act over 'purification' ritual at Mallikarjun Kharge's rally venue in Haldwani
teaser: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi demanded FIR registered SC ST Act against those who allegedly carried out a purification ritual at the venue in Uttarakhand's Haldwani after party president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a rally there.
description: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi demanded FIR registered SC ST Act against those who allegedly carried out a purification ritual at the venue in Uttarakhand's Haldwani after party president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a rally there.
content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has demanded an FIR be registered under the SC/ST Act against those who allegedly carried out a "purification" ritual at a venue in Uttarakhand's Haldwani after party president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a rally there. Kharge addressed a Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani on August 8. Two days later, members of the Shri Ram Sena reportedly conducted a "shuddhikaran" havan at the venue. The Congress alleged that the ritual was aimed at Kharge because he was a Dalit. Rahul Gandhi, speaking at Indira Bhawan in Delhi, said the alleged ritual was offensive under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. "This act violates the SC/ST Act. Performing a 'purification' ritual is a crime. Yet, no action has been taken. Therefore, we demand that an FIR be registered immediately against those who carried out this purification ritual in Uttarakhand," Gandhi said. The Congress leader also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the issue, questioning the BJP leadership's response to the alleged ritual. "The Prime Minister claims to belong to every caste and to be the Prime Minister of all of India. Yet, the chief of his party states that the purification was justified," Gandhi said. "We want the Prime Minister to immediately order the registration of an FIR against these individuals under the SC/ST Act. It is the duty of both the State Government and the Central Government to ensure that Kharge ji receives justice in Uttarakhand," he added. The controversy erupted after a "shuddhikaran" or purification ritual was reportedly conducted at Haldwani's Ramlila Maidan, where Kharge had addressed a Congress rally. The ritual was reportedly held two days later. Congress leaders alleged that it was carried out because Kharge is a Dalit, describing the episode as an instance of caste discrimination. The BJP has denied involvement in the ritual and said the ceremony was a customary religious practice and was not linked to Kharge's visit. Kharge, the Opposition leader in the Rajya Sabha, raised the issue in Parliament. He asked why there was a need for a purification ceremony after his speech. Union minister JP Nadda had called the incident unfortunate, said the BJP did not support such an act and assured the House that the matter would be investigated. The Congress has continued to demand action. A party delegation also met Uttarakhand Governor Lt Gen Gurmit Singh (retd) on August 24, seeking a fair investigation and alleging that no concrete action had been taken despite Nadda's assurance.

title: rahul-gandhi-haldwani-purification-ritual-untouchability-bjp-rss
teaser: Rahul Gandhi targets BJP and RSS over the Haldwani purification ritual after Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally, calling it another form of untouchability.
description: Rahul Gandhi targets BJP and RSS over the Haldwani purification ritual after Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally, calling it another form of untouchability.
content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday accused the BJP and RSS of promoting untouchability after a purification ritual was held at Haldwani’s Ramlila Maidan following Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally. Gandhi said the act was a crime under the Constitution and targeted Dalits while demanding legal action. The BJP has denied involvement, with Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami rejecting it publicly.Also Read: Stop playing that game: Pak-origin US official exposes Islamabad over forced conversion of Hindu girlsRahul Gandhi links Haldwani ritual to untouchabilityAddressing a press conference in Delhi, Gandhi said the controversy reflected a wider political and ideological contest between the Constitution and the ideology of the BJP and RSS.Referring to the ritual at the Haldwani venue, Gandhi said, “Our CLP leader in Rajasthan visits a temple, and BJP leaders perform a purification ritual. Congress President Kharge ji, who has dedicated his entire life to the country and the Constitution, goes to the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani to deliver a speech, and a purification ritual is performed there. Who does this? It is the people from the BJP and RSS.”He added, “Only BJP and RSS members do this, and it is a crime. Under Indias Constitution, this is a crime, a criminal activity. Purification is actually just another name for untouchability. Untouchability was outlawed, yet BJP members practice it openly.”Gandhi said the ritual conveyed that Dalits were being treated as “unclean” and should not be touched. The Congress has alleged that the ritual was linked to Kharge’s Dalit identity. Kharge had earlier raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha and questioned why a purification ceremony was needed after his speech.What happened at the Haldwani rally venueKharge addressed a Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani on August 8, ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand Assembly elections. Two days later, members of the Shri Ram Sena reportedly conducted a “shuddhikaran” havan at the venue. Congress leaders said the ceremony was aimed at Kharge because he is a Dalit.The BJP has denied involvement in the ritual and said the ceremony was a customary religious practice that was not linked to Kharge’s visit. BJP president JP Nadda also said the party did not associate itself with such an act and described the incident as unfortunate.Dhami has also rejected the Congress allegation. He said, “A few organisations protested there over the hurting of religious sentiments; the Congress party attempted to give it a Dalit angle.” He described Kharge as a “highly respectable national leader” and said his insult was “unthinkable”.Kharge has said he did not mention any community or religion during his speech. He later said he did not want the matter to be politicised but demanded strict legal action against those responsible.Also Read: PM Modi’s Central Asia tour: What India wants from Uzbekistan and SCO Article 17 and the law on untouchabilityArticle 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability and prohibits its practice in any form. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 gives effect to this constitutional guarantee and provides punishment for the preaching and practice of untouchability and for disabilities imposed on that basis. The law covers several forms of social and religious discrimination.The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is another important legal framework. It provides for punishment for specified offences against members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and establishes special courts and other protections for victims.However, whether a particular purification ritual amounts to a criminal offence under either law would depend on the facts, the conduct involved and the evidence available. Gandhi’s statement that the act is a crime is a political and legal claim. It is for law enforcement and, where required, courts to determine whether the legal provisions apply.Rahul Gandhi cites wider examples of caste discriminationGandhi used the Haldwani controversy to raise broader concerns about caste discrimination. He said constitutional safeguards had not ended discrimination against Dalits in daily life.“For thousands of years, Dalits in this country have been subjected to atrocities and violence. While the Constitution made this illegal, even today, Dalit children in schools are made to clean toilets and sweep and mop floors,” he said.He also referred to alleged discrimination in access to water and at tea stalls.“Dalits are not allowed to drink water from the village well; they have had to dig their own private wells because they were barred from using the common village well,” Gandhi claimed.He added, “At tea stalls, you see two types of cups in use: a reusable glass cup that can be washed, and a paper or plastic cup that is discarded after use. The plastic or paper cups are for Dalits, while the glass ones are for others,” he alleged.Gandhi said these examples showed why the constitutional ban on untouchability remained an important political and social issue.Haldwani purification row: who says whatStakeholderKey argument or positionCongress and Rahul GandhiCalls the purification ritual another form of untouchability and alleges it was linked to Kharge’s Dalit identity. Gandhi has demanded legal action and an FIR.Mallikarjun KhargeSays he did not mention any community or religion in his speech and questioned why the stage needed to be purified after his rally.BJPDenies involvement in the ritual and says the ceremony was a customary religious practice unrelated to Kharge’s visit. JP Nadda said the BJP does not support such an act.Uttarakhand governmentChief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said independent organisations conducted the ritual and accused Congress of giving the incident a Dalit angle.Legal frameworkArticle 17 abolishes untouchability. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989 provide statutory protections and penalties for specified forms of discrimination and offences.Also Read: We are still searching: Nepal flood turns families’ hope into a desperate wait
article_text: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday accused the BJP and RSS of promoting untouchability after a purification ritual was held at Haldwani’s Ramlila Maidan following Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally. Gandhi said the act was a crime under the Constitution and targeted Dalits while demanding legal action. The BJP has denied involvement, with Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami rejecting it publicly.Also Read: Stop playing that game: Pak-origin US official exposes Islamabad over forced conversion of Hindu girlsRahul Gandhi links Haldwani ritual to untouchabilityAddressing a press conference in Delhi, Gandhi said the controversy reflected a wider political and ideological contest between the Constitution and the ideology of the BJP and RSS.Referring to the ritual at the Haldwani venue, Gandhi said, “Our CLP leader in Rajasthan visits a temple, and BJP leaders perform a purification ritual. Congress President Kharge ji, who has dedicated his entire life to the country and the Constitution, goes to the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani to deliver a speech, and a purification ritual is performed there. Who does this? It is the people from the BJP and RSS.”He added, “Only BJP and RSS members do this, and it is a crime. Under Indias Constitution, this is a crime, a criminal activity. Purification is actually just another name for untouchability. Untouchability was outlawed, yet BJP members practice it openly.”Gandhi said the ritual conveyed that Dalits were being treated as “unclean” and should not be touched. The Congress has alleged that the ritual was linked to Kharge’s Dalit identity. Kharge had earlier raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha and questioned why a purification ceremony was needed after his speech.What happened at the Haldwani rally venueKharge addressed a Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani on August 8, ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand Assembly elections. Two days later, members of the Shri Ram Sena reportedly conducted a “shuddhikaran” havan at the venue. Congress leaders said the ceremony was aimed at Kharge because he is a Dalit.The BJP has denied involvement in the ritual and said the ceremony was a customary religious practice that was not linked to Kharge’s visit. BJP president JP Nadda also said the party did not associate itself with such an act and described the incident as unfortunate.Dhami has also rejected the Congress allegation. He said, “A few organisations protested there over the hurting of religious sentiments; the Congress party attempted to give it a Dalit angle.” He described Kharge as a “highly respectable national leader” and said his insult was “unthinkable”.Kharge has said he did not mention any community or religion during his speech. He later said he did not want the matter to be politicised but demanded strict legal action against those responsible.Also Read: PM Modi’s Central Asia tour: What India wants from Uzbekistan and SCO Article 17 and the law on untouchabilityArticle 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability and prohibits its practice in any form. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 gives effect to this constitutional guarantee and provides punishment for the preaching and practice of untouchability and for disabilities imposed on that basis. The law covers several forms of social and religious discrimination.The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is another important legal framework. It provides for punishment for specified offences against members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and establishes special courts and other protections for victims.However, whether a particular purification ritual amounts to a criminal offence under either law would depend on the facts, the conduct involved and the evidence available. Gandhi’s statement that the act is a crime is a political and legal claim. It is for law enforcement and, where required, courts to determine whether the legal provisions apply.Rahul Gandhi cites wider examples of caste discriminationGandhi used the Haldwani controversy to raise broader concerns about caste discrimination. He said constitutional safeguards had not ended discrimination against Dalits in daily life.“For thousands of years, Dalits in this country have been subjected to atrocities and violence. While the Constitution made this illegal, even today, Dalit children in schools are made to clean toilets and sweep and mop floors,” he said.He also referred to alleged discrimination in access to water and at tea stalls.“Dalits are not allowed to drink water from the village well; they have had to dig their own private wells because they were barred from using the common village well,” Gandhi claimed.He added, “At tea stalls, you see two types of cups in use: a reusable glass cup that can be washed, and a paper or plastic cup that is discarded after use. The plastic or paper cups are for Dalits, while the glass ones are for others,” he alleged.Gandhi said these examples showed why the constitutional ban on untouchability remained an important political and social issue.Haldwani purification row: who says whatStakeholderKey argument or positionCongress and Rahul GandhiCalls the purification ritual another form of untouchability and alleges it was linked to Kharge’s Dalit identity. Gandhi has demanded legal action and an FIR.Mallikarjun KhargeSays he did not mention any community or religion in his speech and questioned why the stage needed to be purified after his rally.BJPDenies involvement in the ritual and says the ceremony was a customary religious practice unrelated to Kharge’s visit. JP Nadda said the BJP does not support such an act.Uttarakhand governmentChief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said independent organisations conducted the ritual and accused Congress of giving the incident a Dalit angle.Legal frameworkArticle 17 abolishes untouchability. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989 provide statutory protections and penalties for specified forms of discrimination and offences.Also Read: We are still searching: Nepal flood turns families’ hope into a desperate wait

title: "What Will Happen To Him?" Nepal Woman Stays Home With Bedridden Husband Despite Flood Alert
teaser: A woman in Nepal's Trishuli Bazaar has refused to leave her home despite a flood alert because her bedridden husband cannot walk, highlighting the challenges faced by vulnerable people during disasters.

title: No surrender, no dissent: How six months of war hardened Iran’s leadership
teaser: Iran's leadership has appointed hard-line military and security officials to key positions. These moves signal a resistance to US pressure and a crackdown on domestic dissent. The new appointments come as Iran faces prolonged confrontation
description: Iran's leadership has appointed hard-line military and security officials to key positions. These moves signal a resistance to US pressure and a crackdown on domestic dissent. The new appointments come as Iran faces prolonged confrontation
content: Six months into its war with the United States and Israel, Iran’s leadership has tightened its grip around a core of hard-line military commanders and clerics, signalling that it will resist US pressure abroad while moving aggressively to prevent dissent at home.A series of senior appointments announced on August 11 and 12 has placed veteran Revolutionary Guard figures and security officials at the heart of Iran’s leadership. The moves come as Tehran prepares for a potentially prolonged confrontation with Washington, rejects trust in negotiations with President Donald Trump and faces mounting economic pressure from the US blockade and new sanctions.The appointments have also made clear that Iran’s rulers are preparing for unrest even as no fresh nationwide protests have emerged. The choice of Hossein Taeb, a veteran intelligence chief who has overseen major crackdowns on protests, to lead the Basij volunteer force is being viewed as a particularly strong warning to potential dissenters.Tehran warns of a wider confrontationIran’s new secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, has adopted a defiant tone towards Washington.“If (Trump) wants to do something, we will retaliate in a seismic manner,” Rezaei said last weekend. In a post on X, he warned that “if the economic war continues, not a single drop of oil will be exported” from the Persian Gulf.His remarks came as Iran faces the prospect of further US military action. Tehran has little faith in reaching a lasting agreement with Trump after coming under attack twice while negotiations were under way. Iranian officials are also believed to be preparing for another possible assault once Washington replenishes its stocks of missile interceptors.The threat of escalation comes alongside an increasingly severe economic squeeze. The US blockade and planned sanctions risk further damaging an economy already struggling with the impact of the war.Rezaei has nevertheless left the door open to negotiations, but only if Washington changes course. On Monday, he told Pakistani mediator Gen. Asim Munir that the US should “change its attitude and take practical action about implementing the conditions” of the ceasefire deal.Hardliners tighten grip around new supreme leaderRezaei’s appointment was part of a wider reshuffle ordered by Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, who has been consolidating his leadership after the death of his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.The elder Khamenei, who had led Iran for about 37 years, was killed in US and Israeli strikes launched on February 28. Much of Iran’s senior leadership was also killed in the bombing campaign.The younger Khamenei, 56, has not appeared publicly or been heard in video or audio since the strikes. He is believed to have been wounded. His continued absence could reflect the extraordinary security measures around him, given that he is likely to remain an Israeli target, or the severity of his injuries.His first major appointments suggest that he is relying heavily on a group of longstanding military and security allies.Rezaei, 71, commanded the Revolutionary Guard during much of its formative period, including the 1980-1988 war with Iraq, and remained in the post until 1997. He has also contested Iran’s presidential election several times as a hard-line candidate.Brig. Gen. Ahmad Vahidi, 68, has been confirmed as head of the Revolutionary Guard after serving as acting commander since his predecessor was killed alongside the elder Khamenei. Gen. Ali Ozmaei and Gen. Ali Abdollahi have also been confirmed in senior military positions.Sascha Bruchmann, an analyst with the International Institute for Strategic Studies’ Middle East office in Bahrain, described the appointments as evidence of an effort to maintain unity at the top.“They are a clique of older senior officers who’ve served together over the last decades,” Bruchmann said.“ It looks like internal cohesion, as in hard core people are being pulled into the inner circle,” he said.Taeb appointment sends warning on dissentPerhaps the clearest indication of Tehran’s domestic priorities is the appointment of Taeb as head of the Basij, the Revolutionary Guard’s volunteer street force.The 63-year-old cleric has a long record of suppressing protests. He led the Basij during the mass demonstrations that followed the disputed 2009 re-election of hard-line president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, when dozens of people were killed.Taeb was later appointed head of the Revolutionary Guard’s intelligence organisation, a position he held for nearly 13 years before being removed in 2022. His departure reportedly followed a shake-up prompted by Israeli espionage successes.The Basij operates a nationwide network of volunteers with a presence in streets, government offices and cultural centres. Its role is to reinforce loyalty to Iran’s theocratic system and promote what the leadership describes as ideological purity.Taeb’s return to a frontline security position suggests that Tehran is preparing to confront discontent before it develops into another mass movement.“Putting someone from an intelligence background in charge of the people that would do the crackdown makes sense,” Bruchmann said.The Basij expanded its presence during the war, while hard-liners have staged nightly rallies in Tehran and other cities. The gatherings have sought to demonstrate support for the government and intimidate potential opponents.In his appointment decree, Khamenei ordered Taeb to expand the Basij’s presence in Iranian social life, make greater use of new technologies and “promote the Basij across the world against Zionist-American arrogance”. The wording could also point to a greater role for the force in building links with Iran’s overseas allies and proxies.Taeb has also warned that US economic pressure is designed to divide Iranian society.“If the mosque becomes the center of the neighborhood, the nation will protect its unity, which will be a greater deterrent than any missile.”Economic crisis exposes divisions inside IranThe leadership’s increasingly hard-line posture comes as ordinary Iranians struggle with the economic consequences of the war.There has so far been no clear sign of a new nationwide protest movement, despite growing difficulties in affording basic goods. But the worsening economic situation has exposed differences within the political establishment over how far Iran should continue confronting Washington.President Masoud Pezeshkian remains one of the most prominent voices advocating a negotiated settlement. His allies have argued that Tehran risks weakening itself by prolonging the conflict while its economy deteriorates.“It would be better to bring the war to an end, since today we enjoy power and dignity and the entire world approved our victory, and the U.S. is hated,” Pezeshkian said last week.He has also defended the June ceasefire agreement, rejecting accusations from hard-liners that it gave away too much.The ceasefire quickly collapsed as the US, Israel and Iran resumed exchanges of strikes. Tehran has since demanded the release of billions of dollars in frozen assets under the agreement, along with formal authority over the Strait of Hormuz.Homayoun Falakshahi, the top oil analyst for global commerce information firm Kpler, said the latest appointments pointed to a tougher approach.The selection of Rezaei and Vahidi showed “greater influence for officials associated with a tougher stance,” he wrote.But he cautioned that escalation carries major risks for Tehran. Iran could struggle to “escalate enough to restore deterrence without triggering retaliation that leaves it worse off”.Iran’s leadership faces a choiceThe emerging power structure therefore presents a stark contrast to Trump’s early hopes that the war could help topple Iran’s Islamic Republic and bring more conciliatory figures to power.Instead, six months of conflict have strengthened the influence of officials with decades of experience in Iran’s military and security establishment.Tehran’s leaders appear determined to maintain confrontation with Washington while ensuring that economic hardship does not translate into political unrest.The result is a leadership that is simultaneously preparing for another possible US attack, threatening retaliation and reinforcing the machinery used to suppress domestic opposition.Tehran-based political analyst Ahmad Zeidabadi said there are “serious differences over the future path of the country”.Hard-liners oppose normalisation with the US because “their survival depends on the existence of conflict and hostility,” he wrote in the newspaper Hammihan, which supports Pezeshkian.For now, the balance of power appears to favour those advocating resistance rather than compromise. Iran’s new leadership is signalling that it will not easily yield to US demands abroad, while showing that dissent at home will face an equally uncompromising response.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Tehran has since demanded the release of billions of dollars in frozen assets under the agreement, along with formal authority over the Strait of Hormuz.Homayoun Falakshahi, the top oil analyst for global commerce information firm Kpler, said the latest appointments pointed to a tougher approach.The selection of Rezaei and Vahidi showed “greater influence for officials associated with a tougher stance,” he wrote.But he cautioned that escalation carries major risks for Tehran. Iran could struggle to “escalate enough to restore deterrence without triggering retaliation that leaves it worse off”.Iran’s leadership faces a choiceThe emerging power structure therefore presents a stark contrast to Trump’s early hopes that the war could help topple Iran’s Islamic Republic and bring more conciliatory figures to power.Instead, six months of conflict have strengthened the influence of officials with decades of experience in Iran’s military and security establishment.Tehran’s leaders appear determined to maintain confrontation with Washington while ensuring that economic hardship does not translate into political unrest.The result is a leadership that is simultaneously preparing for another possible US attack, threatening retaliation and reinforcing the machinery used to suppress domestic opposition.Tehran-based political analyst Ahmad Zeidabadi said there are “serious differences over the future path of the country”.Hard-liners oppose normalisation with the US because “their survival depends on the existence of conflict and hostility,” he wrote in the newspaper Hammihan, which supports Pezeshkian.For now, the balance of power appears to favour those advocating resistance rather than compromise. Iran’s new leadership is signalling that it will not easily yield to US demands abroad, while showing that dissent at home will face an equally uncompromising response.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. title: Dutch institute issues 'red alert' over Trump-shaped ecstasy pills
teaser: The drugs have a delayed effect which "increases the risk of overdose", the institute has advised.
description: The drugs have a delayed effect which "increases the risk of overdose", the institute has advised.
content: Dutch institute issues 'red alert' over Trump-shaped ecstasy pills 15 minutes ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Rorey Bosotti Trimbos Institute "Do not use this pill under any circumstance," the institute warned A Dutch drug addiction and mental health institute has issued a "red alert" to users about potentially lethal ecstasy pills in the shape of US President Donald Trump's head. The Utrecht-based Trimbos Institute said several of the pills had been handed in at testing centres in August and were found to contain a "very high" amount of the chemical PMMA. "Do not use this pill under any circumstance," the institute said in its warning, cautioning that the drug could cause "overheating with potentially fatal consequences". It issued images of the pills, which feature a depiction of Trump's head on one side and the words "Trump" and "NL" stamped on the other. PMMA, or para-methoxymethamfetamine, is a substance similar to MDMA – the active ingredient in ecstasy pills. "However, the effect occurs later, and the stimulating effect is often absent," the institute advised. "This increases the risk of overdose." Users are being warned they could experience symptoms such as nausea, an increased heart rate and convulsions hours after ingesting the pills. Trimbos Institute spokesperson Anniek Groothuis told the Associated Press that it had no reported cases of death or serious illness among possible users. While producing, selling and using ecstasy is illegal in the Netherlands, a 2024 Dutch government report said the substance was "still quite popular as a party drug". The report added that, in 2022, a "record 550,000 people" had taken the drug at least once. This is not the first time Donald Trump's facial features appear to have been used as inspiration for the shape of ecstasy pills. In 2017, German police confiscated about 5,000 carrot-coloured ecstasy tablets in the shape of the US president's head – which they believed had been promoted on the internet under the slogan "Trump makes partying great again". Trimbos Institute The institute released images of two pills - one yellow and blue, and the other red and green Netherlands Donald Trump Europe

title: Legal Notes by Arvind Datar: The Henderson Principle
teaser: Recently, the Supreme Court discussed the Henderson Principle in Celir LLP v. Sumati Prasad Bafna (2024). It often happens that a litigant fails to raise all claims and issues that arise in a particular dispute. In the first round of litiga
description: Recently, the Supreme Court discussed the Henderson Principle in Celir LLP v. Sumati Prasad Bafna (2024). It often happens that a litigant fails to raise all claims and issues that arise in a particular dispute. In the first round of litiga
content: Recently, the Supreme Court discussed the Henderson Principle in Celir LLP v. Sumati Prasad Bafna (2024). It often happens that a litigant fails to raise all claims and issues that arise in a particular dispute. In the first round of litigation, he raises only a few grounds. If he fails, he then tries to raise new issues in a fresh round of litigation. The Henderson Principle dates back to a decision in 1843 - Henderson v. Henderson - wherein the English Chancery Court held that parties to a litigation are required to bring forward and plead their entire case. Two brothers were partners. One brother died and his widow brought proceedings relating to partnership accounts. She was successful in getting a decree that directed the surviving brother to pay GBP 26,650. In the execution proceedings, the surviving brother sought to reopen the accounts and claimed that the deceased brother had overdrawn amounts from the partnership account and nothing was due to his widow. Sir James Vigram, VC, rejected this claim and held that a party will not be permitted to open the same subject to litigation when the facts ought to have been brought forward in the first round of litigation. Once a court of competent jurisdiction has adjudicated the matter in a particular lis, it is not open to the parties to bring forward new grounds that could have been raised on the earlier occasion. The Henderson Principle must not be confused with issue estoppel or constructive res judicata. In Yat Tung Investment Co Ltd v. Dao Heng Bank Ltd (1975), the Privy Council was dealing with an appeal from Hong Kong. The litigant had unsuccessfully made a claim against the bank. The Privy Council held that it would be an abuse of process to permit further action based on another ground that could have been advanced earlier. This principle was discussed once again by the House of Lords in Johnson v Gore Wood & Co (2002). It was held that the Henderson Principle, although separate and distinct from issue estoppel and cause of action estoppel, has much in common with them. It is based on the salutary principle that there should be finality in litigation. If a litigant failed to make a claim or raise a particular defence in the earlier proceeding, it would be an abuse of process if he were allowed to raise a claim or raise that defence in a subsequent litigation. At the same time, the court pointed out that a dogmatic approach should be avoided and that the courts should adopt a broad, merit-based judgment which takes note of the public and private interests involved. The court should consider whether a party is misusing or abusing the process of court by seeking to raise an issue that could have been raised before. Thus, the Henderson Principle has its basis in the principle that there should be finality in litigation. This principle is also reflected in Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, which requires that every suit must include the whole of the claim which the plaintiff is entitled to make in respect of the cause of action. It is submitted that this principle equally applies to writ petitions under Article 226 and to proceedings under taxing statutes as well. If the Income Tax Department is entitled to demand duty from an assessee on various grounds, it must issue the show cause notice on all the grounds. As the Supreme Court pointed out in the Celir LLP case, the parties must ensure that all the grounds of attack or defence are taken in the same proceedings. A party which avoids doing so does it on its own peril. The court will ask the question whether the issue now raised could have been raised earlier. In State of UP v. Nawab Hussain (1977), without referring to the Henderson Principle, the Supreme Court has also emphasised the need to raise all grounds of attack or defence in the concerned dispute or litigation. Public interest requires that an individual should be protected from multiplication of litigation. If the same set of facts gives rise to two or more causes of action, the person cannot be permitted to sue upon one cause of action at one time and reserve the other for subsequent litigation. In this case, a sub-inspector challenged his dismissal by the DIG on the ground that he was not granted a reasonable opportunity of hearing. The writ was dismissed. He then filed a suit claiming that the dismissal by DIG was invalid, as he had been appointed by the IG of Police. The suit was held barred by constructive res judicata as this plea ought to have been taken in the writ petition. The above principle will equally apply when the Department seeks to raise a tax demand on the basis of certain grounds. If these are rejected by the court, it is not open to the Department to issue another notice on the basis of fresh grounds that could have been raised on the earlier occasion. The core component of the Henderson Principle is to prevent abuse of process and prevent the legal system from being exploited in any manner that tends to undermine its integrity. Parties should not be permitted to engage in procedural tactics that fragment and prolong litigation or undermine the outcome of any litigation. It is not a rigid rule but a flexible principle to prevent oppressive, unfair or detrimental litigation. Arvind Datar is a Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court of India. This principle is also reflected in Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, which requires that every suit must include the whole of the claim which the plaintiff is entitled to make in respect of the cause of action. It is submitted that this principle equally applies to writ petitions under Article 226 and to proceedings under taxing statutes as well. If the Income Tax Department is entitled to demand duty from an assessee on various grounds, it must issue the show cause notice on all the grounds. As the Supreme Court pointed out in the Celir LLP case, the parties must ensure that all the grounds of attack or defence are taken in the same proceedings. A party which avoids doing so does it on its own peril. The court will ask the question whether the issue now raised could have been raised earlier. In State of UP v. Nawab Hussain (1977), without referring to the Henderson Principle, the Supreme Court has also emphasised the need to raise all grounds of attack or defence in the concerned dispute or litigation. Public interest requires that an individual should be protected from multiplication of litigation. If the same set of facts gives rise to two or more causes of action, the person cannot be permitted to sue upon one cause of action at one time and reserve the other for subsequent litigation. In this case, a sub-inspector challenged his dismissal by the DIG on the ground that he was not granted a reasonable opportunity of hearing. The writ was dismissed. He then filed a suit claiming that the dismissal by DIG was invalid, as he had been appointed by the IG of Police. The suit was held barred by constructive res judicata as this plea ought to have been taken in the writ petition. The above principle will equally apply when the Department seeks to raise a tax demand on the basis of certain grounds. If these are rejected by the court, it is not open to the Department to issue another notice on the basis of fresh grounds that could have been raised on the earlier occasion. The core component of the Henderson Principle is to prevent abuse of process and prevent the legal system from being exploited in any manner that tends to undermine its integrity. Parties should not be permitted to engage in procedural tactics that fragment and prolong litigation or undermine the outcome of any litigation. It is not a rigid rule but a flexible principle to prevent oppressive, unfair or detrimental litigation. Arvind Datar is a Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court of India. title: Major security breach in Kolkata jail: 3 mobile phones, cash seized from American Centre attack mastermind`s cell
teaser: Kolkata Police seize three mobile phones, Wi-Fi devices, and ₹31,000 cash from the Presidency Jail cell of 2002 American Centre attack mastermind Aftab Ansari.
description: Kolkata Police seize three mobile phones, Wi-Fi devices, and ₹31,000 cash from the Presidency Jail cell of 2002 American Centre attack mastermind Aftab Ansari.
content: The sleuths of the city police's detective department recovered three cell phones with active internet collection and cash from the cell of Aftab Ansari, the mastermind behind the January 2002 attack on the American Centre in Kolkata, the Police informed on Saturday morning. Ansari, an erstwhile operator of the terrorist group, Asif Reza Commando (ARC), which had ties with Pakistan-based militant outfits such as Harkat-ul-Jihad-e-Islami (HUJI) and Jaish-e-Mohammed. (JeM), is currently serving life imprisonment at Presidency Central Correctional Home in South Kolkata. Recently, it came to the notice of the detective department sleuths that mobile communications were being made from the cell of Ansari at Presidency Jail, multiple times in a day. Accordingly, city police sources said, a sudden raid and search operations were conducted at his cell by the detective department sleuths. “Three mobile phones, two routers, a WIFI device, two card readers, a pen drive, and earphones were recovered from his clothes and beddings. At the same time, the detective department sleuths Rs 31,000, all in Rs 500-denominations, from Ansari’s possession. An investigation has been launched into how such items reached the cell of a notorious terrorist like Ansari, who is currently serving life imprisonment,” said a city police officer. He said that the raid and search operations at Ansari’s cell were conducted on Friday night. A case had already been registered at the local Hasting Police Station and on the basis of that an investigation had been initiated. The investigating officers are not ruling out the possibility of involvement of prison officials and staff behind the development. It is leant that the main focus of investigation in the matter is persons or places where Ansari used to communicate by using these devices. The sleuths are especially trying to trace whether he was communicating with anyone in Pakistan or not and what were the communication channels that he had been using for that purpose. Earlier, a similar raid and search operations were conducted at the Presidency Central Correctional Home on August 20. A smartphone and a SIM card were recovered from undertrial prisoner Abdul Moinuddin on that day. During the recent past, several actions have been initiated by the state administration to snap the prison official-criminal nexus in the state. Recently, the superintendent and chief controller of Presidency Central Correctional Home were also suspended. The Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari also ordered a Criminal Investigation Department (CID) probe in the matter. hindi_script: कोलकाता के साउथ स्थित प्रेसिडेंसी सेंट्रल करेक्शनल होम में बंद साल 2002 के अमेरिकन सेंटर हमले के मास्टरमाइंड आफताब अंसारी के सेल पर कोलकाता पुलिस के डिटेक्टिव डिपार्टमेंट ने शुक्रवार रात अचानक छापेमारी की। इस दौरान अंसारी के कपड़ों और बिस्तरों से एक्टिव इंटरनेट वाले तीन मोबाइल फोन, दो राउटर, एक वाई-फाई डिवाइस, दो कार्ड रीडर, एक पेन ड्राइव और इयरफोन बरामद हुए। इसके साथ ही पुलिस ने अंसारी के पास से 500-500 रुपये के नोटों में 31 हजार रुपये नकद भी जब्त किए। आफताब अंसारी आतंकी संगठन आसिफ रजा कमांडो (ARC) का पूर्व ऑपरेटर रहा है, जिसके तार पाकिस्तान स्थित हरकत-उल-जिहाद-अल-इस्लामी (HUJI) और जैश-ए-मोहम्मद (JeM) जैसे आतंकी गुटों से जुड़े थे। वह फिलहाल उम्रकैद की सजा काट रहा है। डिटेक्टिव डिपार्टमेंट को जानकारी मिली थी कि अंसारी के सेल से दिन में कई बार मोबाइल पर बातचीत की जा रही है। इसके बाद स्थानीय हेस्टिंग्स पुलिस स्टेशन में मामला दर्ज कर जांच शुरू की गई। जांच अधिकारी इस बात की पड़ताल कर रहे हैं कि इतने कुख्यात आतंकी तक ये सामान कैसे पहुंचे और इसमें जेल अधिकारियों या कर्मचारियों की क्या भूमिका रही। पुलिस का मुख्य फोकस यह पता लगाना है कि अंसारी इन उपकरणों से किन लोगों के संपर्क में था और क्या उसने पाकिस्तान में भी किसी से बातचीत की है। इससे पहले 20 अगस्त को इसी प्रेसिडेंसी सेंट्रल करेक्शनल होम में तलाशी के दौरान विचाराधीन कैदी अब्दुल मोइनुद्दीन से एक स्मार्टफोन और सिम कार्ड बरामद हुआ था। राज्य में जेल प्रशासन और अपराधियों की साठगांठ को खत्म करने के लिए हाल ही में प्रेसिडेंसी जेल के सुपरिंटेंडेंट और चीफ कंट्रोलर को निलंबित किया जा चुका है, जबकि चीफ मिनिस्टर सुवेन्दु अधिकारी ने इस मामले में सीआईडी (CID) जांच के आदेश दिए हैं।

title: NLU Delhi student body expresses solidarity with NLSIU students over cancelled convocation
teaser: The governing council of the student bar council at National Law University, Delhi (NLUD) has expressed solidarity with the graduating batch of National Law School of India University (NLSIU) after their convocation was cancelled.The August
description: The governing council of the student bar council at National Law University, Delhi (NLUD) has expressed solidarity with the graduating batch of National Law School of India University (NLSIU) after their convocation was cancelled.The August
content: The governing council of the student bar council at National Law University, Delhi (NLUD) has expressed solidarity with the graduating batch of National Law School of India University (NLSIU) after their convocation was cancelled. The August 28 statement from the student body recognises the importance of the Chief Justice of India's (CJI) association with the convocation given that he is the ex-officio Chancellor of NLSIU. However, it argues that at the same time, concerns and views expressed by graduating students should not have resulted in the cancellation of the convocation itself. "A graduating batch must have the autonomy and freedom to express its collective views on matters concerning its convocation, including regarding the invitation of guests to the ceremony. The statement notes that NLSIU occupies a significant place in the Indian legal education landscape and remains the institution that countless aspiring law students dream of attending. "Its (NLSIU's) stature carries with it a corresponding responsibility to uphold the values of academic freedom, student autonomy, and constitutional expression that are central to the legal education it seeks to impart. "We therefore urge the University to reconsider the decision and explore an arrangement that respects the position of the Chancellor while also respecting the graduating students," it said. However, things took a turn on August 15, when over 700 members of the NLSIU community signed a statement objecting to BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra and CJI Surya Kant attending NLSIU's convocation. It was then understood that students had agreed to attend the convocation after they were assured that BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra would not attend the function. However, a notice dated August 27 announced that no convocation would be held due to "unavoidable circumstances" and that students would be conferred their degrees in absentia. It later emerged that the convocation was cancelled after the students rejected a demand by the university authorities to issue a public statement inviting CJI Surya Kant to the ceremony. title: At least 27 dead and hundreds evacuated after strikes near Kyiv
teaser: A 14-year-old girl is among the dead after an attack near the capital overnight, the region's governor said.
description: A 14-year-old girl is among the dead after an attack near the capital overnight, the region's governor said.
content: At least 27 dead and hundreds evacuated after strikes near Kyiv 18 minutes ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Rorey Bosotti Reuters Smoke could be seen rising near a residential area in the Kyiv region early on Saturday Twenty-seven people have been killed in an overnight drone strike on the Kyiv region, its governor has confirmed. Tymur Tkachenko said a further 42 people, including four children, were injured in the Russian attack on the Bucha district. A further 381 people have been evacuated. Search and rescue operations were ongoing early on Saturday as emergency services inspected buildings for damage. Tkachenko later added that a 14-year-old was killed in a separate attack in the Boryspil district. "This is yet another victim of Russian terror," he said. President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed his condolences to the families of the victims, saying that more than 300 emergency respondents had been deployed to the strike area. Zelensky also reported further overnight strikes in the regions of Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy and Zaporizhzhia. "Ukraine cannot be alone in finding solutions to protect against such strikes, and I thank everyone who helps with additional support packages and sanctions against Russia," he wrote on Telegram. The Ukrainian army said it had shot down 233 Russia unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) overnight into Saturday. Russia and Ukraine have been intensifying their attacks in recent months, with Kyiv focusing its operations on Russian economic targets. In the past 24 hours, Moscow has reported strikes on the Belgorod and Rostov regions. Rostov Governor Yuri Slusar said seven people were injured in the attack. Ukraine Russia Europe

title: Nepal Flash Floods: 404 people from Maharashtra stranded in Nepal-Tibet, 60 still untraceable
teaser: More than 404 people from Maharashtra are stranded in the Nepal-Tibet region due to flash floods. Authorities contacted 338 individuals and ensured their well-being, with 37 being shifted back to India, according to a report from the Mahara
description: More than 404 people from Maharashtra are stranded in the Nepal-Tibet region due to flash floods. Authorities contacted 338 individuals and ensured their well-being, with 37 being shifted back to India, according to a report from the Mahara
content: More than 404 people from Maharashtra are stranded in the Nepal-Tibet region due to flash floods. Authorities contacted 338 individuals and ensured their well-being, with 37 being shifted back to India, according to a report from the Maharashtra government on Saturday. With over 404 people from Maharashtra stranded in the Nepal-Tibet region following flash floods, authorities have contacted 338 people and ensured their well-being. "37 of them are being shifted to India," a Maharashtra government report said on Saturday. However, 60 tourists who had reached Nepal through Mumbai-based Richa Tour are still untraceable. The flash floods swept through Rasuwa and other parts of central Nepal on Wednesday, causing loss of life and widespread damage to settlements, roads, bridges and hydropower infrastructure, while leaving nearly 2,000 people missing. The report said the Ministry of External Affairs has provided a list of 149 Indians - all from different districts of Maharashtra and currently safe in the China/Tibet region to the state government. The government has forwarded the list to all the district collectors for identification and further coordination, according to the report. "As many as 105 citizens from Nagpur have already returned to India, and they are among the 404 people who were reported safe," it said. The report said 60 citizens had travelled to Nepal through Mumbai-based Richa Tours Pvt Ltd and authorities had not yet established direct contact with this group. Information about six other citizens was received through an online link, but officials could not contact them either. The State Emergency Operations Centre (SEOC) is coordinating with the MEA control room and regularly sending updated lists. Rescue teams have been deployed at the affected locations as required, while efforts to trace missing citizens are underway. District authorities are verifying information about stranded citizens, while officials are maintaining contact with travel agencies and family members through helplines.

title: Uttar Pradesh STF arrests two wanted criminals hiding in Lucknow, Pune
teaser: The arrest followed surveillance by an STF team deployed in the Lucknow commissionerate to track wanted criminals.
description: The arrest followed surveillance by an STF team deployed in the Lucknow commissionerate to track wanted criminals.
content: The Uttar Pradesh STF arrested two wanted criminals in separate intelligence-based operations after tracking them to locations outside their home districts, officials said on Saturday. One, carrying a ₹50,000 reward, was arrested in Lucknow in connection with a case in Azamgarh, while another, also carrying a ₹50,000 reward and wanted in a murder case in Unnao, was arrested in Pune. The arrests highlight the STF’s intensified efforts to track wanted and reward-declared criminals who move to other districts or states to evade arrest. In Lucknow, the STF arrested Pramod Kumar, a resident of Azamgarh, near Globe Park in the Qaiserbagh area around 5.30 pm on Friday. Kumar was wanted in a case registered at Kotwali Nagar police station in Azamgarh under the Uttar Pradesh Gangsters Act, and a ₹50,000 reward had been announced for information leading to his arrest. The arrest followed surveillance by an STF team deployed in the Lucknow commissionerate to track wanted criminals. Officials said an informer tipped off the team that Pramod would arrive at Globe Park to meet an acquaintance. The STF alerted local police and kept the area under surveillance. Pramod was identified and arrested after the informer confirmed his identity. During interrogation, Pramod allegedly told the STF that he had been hiding in Lucknow to evade arrest in the Gangsters Act case. According to the STF, 12 criminal cases are registered against him under various laws, including the IPC, BNS, Arms Act, Gangsters Act and Excise Act. His criminal record dates back to 2009, with several cases also registered in 2024. In the second operation, the STF arrested Rafiq Qureshi alias Lalli, who was wanted in a murder case in Unnao, in Pune on Thursday. Qureshi, a resident of Turiqiya village under Gangaghat police station in Unnao, was arrested near Heritage Hotel in the Kharadi area around 9.15 am. He was wanted in an FIR from 2025, registered at Achalganj police station under Sections 3(5), 103(1) and 238 of the BNS. A ₹50,000 reward had been declared for his arrest. He was wanted in connection with an FIR registered at Achalganj police station in 2025 under Sections 3(5), 103(1) and 238 of the BNS. A ₹50,000 reward had been announced for information leading to his arrest. According to the STF, Qureshi allegedly confessed to killing Imran alias Kale of Achalganj on July 6, 2025, with the help of Farman alias Chunna. He allegedly fled to Pune after his name surfaced during the investigation and began working as a pickup-loader driver. Qureshi was produced before a court in Pune, which granted his transit remand. He was subsequently brought to Unnao and handed over to Achalganj police for further legal proceedings. title: Haiti gang frees 13 women and children days after raid that killed at least 47 people
teaser: A gang in Haiti has freed thirteen hostages, including women and children, following a brutal assault. UNICEF played a crucial role in securing their release from a farming community. This incident in Kenscoff underscores the rampant violen
description: A gang in Haiti has freed thirteen hostages, including women and children, following a brutal assault. UNICEF played a crucial role in securing their release from a farming community. This incident in Kenscoff underscores the rampant violen
content: A violent Haitian gang has released 13 hostages — seven women and six children — from among 50 people it kidnapped nearly a week ago when it launched a deadly attack on a farming community near the capital, Port-au-Prince.Unicef, the United Nations’ children’s agency that helped secure their release, said late Friday that those freed included three children under the age of two, a seven-year-old child, and two teenage girls.According to Unicef, it worked with leaders of Kenscoff, the targeted farming settlement, to help secure the release of the women and children. It was not immediately clear whether they needed medical treatment or whether more women and children remained in captivity.“This release offers a rare moment of hope amid the violence threatening children in Haiti. The Kenscoff abduction was not an isolated incident but another stark reminder of the scale and frequency of attacks on children across the country,” Yannig Dussart, Unicef’s deputy representative in the Caribbean nation, told The Associated Press.Gangs killed at least 47 people during the August 23 attack on Kenscoff, a once-peaceful farming community in the hills above Port-au-Prince.A gang leader known as Izo 2 had threatened to execute all the hostages if police killed any gang members during their efforts to secure the abductees. Izo 2 leads an armed group in the area on behalf of, and in coordination with, other gang leaders, including Izo, who is considered one of Haiti’s most powerful gang leaders.UN estimates show that attacks in Kenscoff over two months in early 2025 killed more than 260 people and resulted in the destruction or burning of 200 homes. Around 3,000 people were forced to flee. Nearly a dozen further attacks have occurred since then, involving rape, kidnapping, arson and livestock theft.The neighbourhood overlooks routes leading to Petion-Ville, where several embassies, upscale hotels and the temporary seat of government are located. It also overlooks a major road connecting the capital with southern Haiti.While individual kidnappings are commonplace in Haiti, mass abductions are less common. Their outcomes vary: Some hostages are released without a ransom being paid, while others are killed despite multiple ransom payments.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. title: Uttar Pradesh on H1N1 alert, 551 cases reported across 57 districts
teaser: Deputy chief minister Brajesh Pathak asks hospitals to set up separate OPDs, keep beds, supplies ready
description: Deputy chief minister Brajesh Pathak asks hospitals to set up separate OPDs, keep beds, supplies ready
content: “In districts reporting a high incidence of flu and fever, instructions have been issued to set up separate OPDs for such patients,” said deputy chief minister Brajesh Pathak said this during a review meeting on swine flu preparedness across all 75 districts on Saturday. He also directed that people from flood-hit Nepal requiring medical treatment be provided care on priority, while vigil has been stepped up in border districts to monitor severe acute respiratory illness (SARI) cases. A total of 31,478 H1N1 cases have been reported across the country, including 551 in Uttar Pradesh. As many as 57 districts in the state have reported H1N1 infections, with six recording cases in double digits. Gautam Buddh Nagar has reported the highest number of cases at 189, followed by Lucknow (113), Meerut (54) and Ghaziabad (32). These four districts account for nearly 70% of the state’s total cases. Muzaffarnagar and Bulandshahr have reported 11 and 10 cases, respectively, state surveillance officer Dr Vikasendu Agrawal said during the meeting. Pathak directed hospitals to ensure adequate stocks of medicines, oxygen, nebulisers, oxygen masks and bronchodilators. Separate OPDs for patients with respiratory complaints will facilitate screening, consultation and treatment while also helping reduce congestion at hospitals. Pathak directed that four to six isolation beds be kept ready at district and combined hospitals in every district to treat critical patients. Given the number of patients in the state, instructions have been issued to ensure hospitals in all districts remain fully prepared and resources are monitored regularly. All critically ill patients admitted with symptoms such as breathing difficulties should be tested for flu. The health department said people who have been in contact with patients suffering from influenza-like illnesses or respiratory infections should be started on antiviral medication promptly, as advised by doctors, if they develop symptoms. The deputy CM also directed officials to educate patients and attendants at hospitals about the importance of wearing masks, maintaining hand hygiene and following proper cough etiquette. The deputy chief minister also inspected the HOPE (Health Online Parameter Evaluation) monitoring system at the health directorate in the presence of additional chief secretary (Medical and Health) Amit Kumar Ghosh, director general of medical and health services Dr Pawan Kumar Arun and state surveillance officer Dr Vikasendu Agrawal. Published - August 29, 2026 08:14 pm IST - KALABURAGI Newly elected Mayor Ajmal Ahmed Gola and Deputy Mayor Farhanaz Khusro Jahagirdar at the Kalaburagi City Corporation on Saturday. | Photo Credit: ARUN KULKARNI The ruling Congress strengthened its grip on the Kalaburagi City Corporation on Saturday, with Ajmal Ahmed Gola and Farhanaz Khusro Jahagirdar winning the Mayor and Deputy Mayor elections, respectively, giving the party a fresh mandate to lead the civic body for its 24th term. Mr. Gola, a councillor from Ward 21, and Ms. Farhanaz, a councillor from Ward 20, secured 35 votes each. The 55-member corporation requires 33 votes for a simple majority. The BJP councillors, Gururaj Pattan and Meghana Kalaskar, who contested for the Mayor and Deputy Mayor posts, respectively, polled 29 votes each. The election was closely watched within the Congress, with several councillors expressing interest in the Mayor’s post. Former Mayor Syed Ahmed and Ali Khan, the brother of former Minister Rahim Khan, were among those who had expressed interest in the post, along with Mr. Gola. The choice of Mr. Gola followed brief discussions and consultations with Congress councillors, involving district in-charge Minister Priyank Kharge, Radhakrishna Doddamani, MP, and MLAs Kaneez Fatima and Allamprabhu Patil. The consultations helped the party arrive at a common choice and present a united front in the election. Kalaburagi Regional Commissioner Zaheera Naseem, who was the election officer, conducted the election process. The election was originally scheduled for August 7 but was postponed owing to unforeseen circumstances. The Regional Commissioner issued a revised notification fixing August 29 as the date for the election. Mr. Doddamani, Ms. Fatima, Mr. Patil, Basavaraj Mattimadu, MLA, and MLCs Jagadev Guttedar, B.G. Patil, Thippannappa Kamaknoor, and Chandrashekhar Patil Humnabad were present during the election process. Though the BJP and the JD(S) are allies in the State, the councillors of the two parties failed to ensure effective coordination during the corporation election. Speaking to the press after his election, Mr. Gola thanked the party leadership and Congress councillors for their support. He said his immediate focus would be on improving garbage disposal and drinking water supply, upgrading roads, and strengthening property tax collection. He also said the corporation would identify encroachments on its properties and take appropriate action against those responsible. Published - August 29, 2026 08:14 pm IST - Mumbai Government of Maharashtra should survey crops that may have dried up due to inadequate rainfall said Dharashiv MP from Shiv Sena Omprakash Raje Nimbalkar. He demanded compensation and financial aid for the eligible farmers in the Marathwada region. Mr. Nimbalkar sent a letter to Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. In the letter, he said that there has been almost no rainfall in the region of Marathwada for the past 45 days. “The soybean crop has dried due to lack of water. Farmers have faced a financial loss due to this and are in trouble. The situation is serious, and surveys should be conducted through the revenue and agriculture departments to ascertain the losses. Published - August 29, 2026 08:12 pm IST - AMARAVATI The JAC leader is portraying the dues inherited from the previous YSRCP government as liabilities created by the NDA dispensation, while ignoring the funds released during the last two years, says Revenue Minister Anagani Satya Prasad. | Photo Credit: File Photo Revenue Minister Anagani Satya Prasad on Saturday charged Bopparaju Venkateswarlu, APJAC Amaravati chairman and A.P. Revenue Services Association president, with provoking employees and damaging the relationship between the government and its workforce. “Is Mr. Venkateswarlu focusing on resolving employees’ problems or pursuing a political agenda?” the Revenue Minister questioned. The JAC leader was portraying the dues inherited from the previous YSRCP government as liabilities created by the NDA dispensation, while ignoring the funds released during the last two years, Mr. Satya Prasad said in a press release. “The government is holding discussions with Mr. Venkateswarlu and other employee unions, and is fully committed to resolving the issues despite financial constraints,” the Revenue Minister said, adding that a majority of the bills kept pending by the previous government had been cleared, and the remaining would be cleared in phases. Mr. Satya Prasad said the government had extended the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) to 11,000 CPS employees and restored the contributions allegedly diverted by the previous government. Pending bills of retired employees had also been fully cleared, the Minister asserted. Objecting to the manner in which the JAC leader conducted a meeting recently, the Minister said, “While there is no objection to staging protests or questioning the government, humiliating the Chief Minister will not be tolerated.” Copyright© 2026, THG PUBLISHING PVT LTD. or its affiliated companies. title: Karnataka CID arrests IAS officer Gangwar in KPSC exam irregularities case
teaser: The Karnataka CID arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in a probe into alleged KPSC exam irregularities, including OMR manipulation and marks tampering.
description: The Karnataka CID arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in a probe into alleged KPSC exam irregularities, including OMR manipulation and marks tampering.
content: The Karnataka CID has arrested Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in connection with alleged irregularities in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) examination for 400 veterinary officer posts, officials said. Gangwar, a former KPSC examination controller, was taken into custody late Saturday night after several hours of questioning in a probe into alleged question paper leakage, OMR sheet manipulation and marks tampering. Investigators found inconsistencies in his statements and felt he was not cooperating with the inquiry. He is expected to be produced before a magistrate on Sunday, officials aware of the development said. Gangwar was questioned for about nine hours in Bengaluru on Friday before the interrogation continued on Saturday, officials said, adding that investigators are examining his role in the conduct of the examination, including the handling of question papers, evaluation and alleged manipulation of OMR answer sheets. The FIR alleges that Gangwar received ₹1.1 crore from two candidates in return for tampering with their OMR sheets. He was booked under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 10 of the Karnataka Public Examination (Measures for Prevention of Corruption & Unfair Means in Recruitment) Act. The government transferred the case to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) on July 28 after two cases were registered at the Vidhana Soudha police station. The complaint was filed by veterinarian Manjunath against suspended former KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa S Sahukara and others. Manjunath alleged that relatives of the former chairman, KPSC members and staff obtained unusually high marks in the examination conducted on January 8 and 9 despite having average academic records. He also alleged that some candidates who had cleared national-level competitive examinations performed poorly in the state recruitment test. The complaint raised further questions about the conduct of candidates before the examination. Some candidates alleged that shortlisted aspirants switched off their mobile phones before or on the examination days and stayed at hotels and resorts outside Karnataka, where intermediaries allegedly provided them with the questions. Manjunath also questioned the authenticity of OMR answer sheets. He alleged that candidates who had left several questions unanswered nevertheless secured high marks, while intermediaries offered to manipulate OMR sheets for up to ₹80 lakh. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) is separately examining the alleged recruitment irregularities. On August 23, the agency searched Gangwar’s residence in Jayamahal Extension, Bengaluru. Officials said Gangwar was in Uttar Pradesh when the search took place and that officials allegedly entered the residence using a duplicate key. Gangwar had also come under attention earlier this month after he remained out of contact for two days from August 20. He later contacted the government and said he had gone to his hometown because of a family emergency. Home minister Priyank Kharge subsequently said that no IAS officer had gone missing. Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.

title: Iceland EU referendum on a knife edge as counting continues
teaser: A vote on whether to resume membership talks with the European Union is too close to call.
description: A vote on whether to resume membership talks with the European Union is too close to call.
content: Iceland EU referendum on a knife edge as counting continues IMAGE SOURCE, REUTERS Image caption, Iceland's Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir votes in the referendum in Reykjavik Published 1 hour ago By Chris Graham Iceland's closely fought referendum on whether to resume membership talks with the European Union is going down to wire, with the result too close to call. Based on the first 153,197 votes counted of the 270,000 voters eligible, 50.1% rejected the government's proposal, while 49.9% said yes, public broadcaster RUV said, with just 435 votes splitting them. Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir's centre-left government promised to hold a referendum by 2027, but brought it forward because of international tensions, including US President Donald Trump's threats against Greenland. However, debate in this island nation of almost 400,000 people centred more on its fishing industry rather than security concerns. Already part of the EU's single market and Schengen border-free zone, EU membership would bring Iceland into the customs union and eventually the euro. Iceland began its application to join the EU in 2009 in the wake of the 2008 financial crisis and the collapse of Iceland's banking system. Its application was already well advanced when a eurosceptic government came to power in 2013 and put talks on hold. Fishing rights was the biggest obstacle then - as it remains today. Fish and marine industries account for almost 40% of Iceland's exports and many No voters feared they would cede some control of their lucrative fishing grounds under the EU's common fisheries policy. The referendum campaign has fuelled debate about Iceland's place in the world, Frostadottir said after casting her ballot in the capital on Saturday. "This is a great day, we've been waiting for this for years to be able to have a vote," Frostadottir said, adding that her government would continue its work regardless of the outcome. The question on the ballot was: "Should Iceland resume accession negotiations with the European Union?" A Yes vote would not be a final decision on joining the EU, but a move towards an accession agreement, which would then have to be approved by a second referendum. Equally, the No vote would not rule out the chance of Iceland resuming talks in the future. While economic issues dominated the referendum campaigns, security concerns also featured. Iceland is a founder member of Nato but it has no military and relies on its allies for defence. The country has backed Ukraine during Russia's full-scale invasion and officials have been alarmed by Russia's increased maritime manoeuvres near the island. Trump's expressed interest in taking over Greenland has also raised concerns. Related topics Iceland Europe European Union
